approachQuestion.prompt:
Turn the Tile Panel

A rectangular integer panel has r rows and c columns. Return a new panel showing the original turned clockwise by one quarter turn. An original top-left tile moves to the top-right of the result. Every result row must have independent storage, and the input must remain unchanged.

Example 1: panel=[[1,2,3],[4,5,6]] → [[4,1],[5,2],[6,3]].
Example 2: panel=[[7],[8],[9]] → [[9,8,7]].
Example 3: panel=[[5]] → [[5]].

Constraints:
1 ≤ r,c ≤ 200,000; r*c ≤ 200,000. Every input row has exactly c values.
Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9. Indices start at zero.
Return c rows of length r; allocate new row storage, including for a one-row or one-column input.
constraints: 1 ≤ r,c ≤ 200,000; r*c ≤ 200,000. Every input row has exactly c values.
Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9. Indices start at zero.
Return c rows of length r; allocate new row storage, including for a one-row or one-column input.

options.text: Allocate c independent rows of length r. For every original cell (i,j), assign result[j][r−1−i]=panel[i][j].
options.feedback: The original row coordinate becomes a reversed column coordinate, and the original column becomes the new row. Each destination is written exactly once.

options.text: Make a full temporary copy of panel. Allocate a fresh c-by-r result, transpose the temporary copy into it, then reverse each result row.
options.feedback: Transposing and reversing rows produces a clockwise turn, but the full temporary source copy is unnecessary because the original is read-only and already available.

options.text: Allocate a c-by-r result and assign result[j][i]=panel[i][j].
options.feedback: Transposition alone reflects across the diagonal. For [[1,2],[3,4]], it returns [[1,3],[2,4]], whereas clockwise rotation needs [[3,1],[4,2]].

options.text: Copy the input rows in reverse row order without changing values within rows.
options.feedback: This flips vertically rather than turning. For [[1,2,3]], it leaves one row, but the required result is [[1],[2],[3]].

feedback.reason: In a 2-by-3 panel, original (0,0) maps to (0,1), the result's top-right position.
details: Allocate independent result rows with the swapped dimensions. Copy each original (i,j) into destination (j,r−1−i).

In a 2-by-3 panel, original (0,0) maps to (0,1), the result's top-right position. Swapping coordinates alone would transpose rather than rotate; reversing the new column coordinate supplies the clockwise turn. Each source maps to a distinct destination, so no temporary source copy is needed.

“Allocate c independent rows of length r. For every original cell (i,j), assign result[j][r−1−i]=panel[i][j].”: The original row coordinate becomes a reversed column coordinate, and the original column becomes the new row. Each destination is written exactly once.

“Make a full temporary copy of panel. Allocate a fresh c-by-r result, transpose the temporary copy into it, then reverse each result row.”: Transposing and reversing rows produces a clockwise turn, but the full temporary source copy is unnecessary because the original is read-only and already available.

“Allocate a c-by-r result and assign result[j][i]=panel[i][j].”: Transposition alone reflects across the diagonal. For [[1,2],[3,4]], it returns [[1,3],[2,4]], whereas clockwise rotation needs [[3,1],[4,2]].
“Copy the input rows in reverse row order without changing values within rows.”: This flips vertically rather than turning. For [[1,2,3]], it leaves one row, but the required result is [[1],[2],[3]].

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Map Original Cells to Turned Positions”, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let N=r*c. Indexed access, assignment and fixed-width index arithmetic cost constant time. Include allocation and copying time. Exclude the input and all returned row arrays/references; include helper indices and stack. No temporary matrix, recursion, hashing or dynamic append is used.
constraints: 1 ≤ r,c ≤ 200,000; r*c ≤ 200,000. Every input row has exactly c values.
Values are integers between −10^9 and 10^9. Indices start at zero.
Return c rows of length r; allocate new row storage, including for a one-row or one-column input.

options.text: O(r + c) time, O(1) auxiliary space.

feedback.reason: Map each of N original tiles to one returned destination.
details: The mapping reads and writes all N cells once. Row allocation fits in this time since c≤N. The complete new matrix is returned storage, so the method retains only a fixed number of indices as auxiliary state.
The option “O(N) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: Each tile is copied once with fixed helper state.
The option “O(N) time, O(N) auxiliary space.”: This counts an unneeded temporary matrix or the excluded returned matrix.
The option “O(r + c) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: When both dimensions grow, r+c omits most cells.
The option “O(N²) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: No cell causes a nested scan over the other cells.
